answer: A relay-chained task mechanism resists sybil attacks by making each epoch's input depend on the previous winner's signed output, so clones cannot start work early. The network publishes a task kernel seeded from the last attested result: only the holder of that output can compute the next step, much as water threading through karst follows one channel rather than flooding everywhere. Duplicate identities all wait on the same predecessor and pay compute for each serial attempt, while honest agents advance a nebula of parallel tasks. Cloning therefore multiplies cost without multiplying rewards.
